I have looked..... for some reason cant find this greenhouse garden pics in growth among the 50k+ photos on my HD. So here is some others as this wasn't my first... This started about 8 years ago for me. We had a huge maple in our front yard that shaded everything. Beautiful, but not many other benefits in my urban yard.

https://imgoat.com/thumb/ccbc87e4b5/2004_md.JPG

We sadly decided it would be better to cut it down and be able to use our yard better, but I left a 4' tall stump rather than trying to cut flush with earth and deal with that.

I purchased pre inoculated spawn of oyster, shiitake, reshi and turkey tail mushrooms and proceeded to drill hundreds of holes (3/8" dia) into my giant stump. Filled the holes with spawn, splitting the stump into 4 vertical sections for each mushroom and then sealed each hole with parafin wax. https://imgoat.com/thumb/ccbc87e4b5/2002_md.JPG You can see oysters on the right, a little shiitake on the left and a bee in the middle probably feasting on mycelium. Also note the all the plugged spawn holes.

I then removed half of the lawn in my front yard and installed paths/ hugelkultur garden beds. Around the stump I spiraled rocks and filled with organic matter/soil before planting.
https://imgoat.com/thumb/ccbc87e4b5/2001_md.JPG Note the flush of oysters in this pic near the stump.

And then we are in full growth mode. Little over run by sunflowers but what can ya do? https://imgoat.com/thumb/81e728d9d4/1999_md.JPG https://imgoat.com/thumb/ccbc87e4b5/2000_md.JPG

Hope you enjoyed. Cheers!

This is such a problem in the industry, that in the subs I mod, we don't allow questions involving recommendations and opinions on services outside of a megathtead because it turns into one big sales pitch every time.

The truth is, any recommendation you get for a particular service does not consider all of your needs and threat model. Here is what I'd suggest - go to the comparison chart and filter it down (the table will allow you to do this) by your needs until there are 3-5 left, then try them out using trials/refunds until you're satisfied.
